input: nums is a dense ordinary Array of primitive safe-integer Number values, excluding negative zero, with 0 <= nums.length <= 10 and all values in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. Duplicate values are permitted, and input order is arbitrary. Sparse arrays, accessors, proxies, boxed values, NaN, infinities, fractions, BigInt and concurrent mutation are excluded. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. The bounded length limits recursive helper depth to n + 1 <= 11 live calls; unbounded recursion or output capacity is not claimed.
return: A fresh Array of fresh Array subsets, including one empty subset first. Every distinct submultiset appears exactly once, with each value used no more often than its input multiplicity. Each subset is in ascending numeric order. Subsets are emitted by depth-first increasing-sorted-index traversal, recording each path before extending it and skipping equal siblings at the same recursion depth. Empty input returns a one-element outer sequence containing a fresh empty sequence. The output sequence is deterministic and must agree exactly between these paired candidates on their shared domain, independently of order-insensitive problem acceptance.
mutation_aliasing: The input Array, its order and all entries remain unchanged. Sorting operates only on a fresh shallow copy, never on nums. Each returned subset is a fresh shallow copy of the temporary path, and all elements are immutable integers. The outer result, each inner subset, nums and the temporary path are distinct mutable containers; no returned subset aliases another. Mutating one returned subset cannot change any other subset or the input. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: The shared length bound is 0 <= n <= 10, and each value is an integer in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. Values are copied, not arithmetically transformed; indices, depth and index + 1 remain exact safe integers. Python arbitrary-size integers do not broaden the paired value domain. The JavaScript numeric comparator uses relational comparisons and returns only -1, 0 or 1 rather than subtracting two potentially extreme safe integers. The maximum output count is 2^10 = 1024 subsets; duplicates only reduce it.
complexity: Let n be input length and U = product(m_i + 1) over the distinct-value multiplicities, with empty product 1. Backtracking takes O((n + 1)*U) time including duplicate-skipping scans and copied output, and O(n + 1) auxiliary path/stack space. Retained output uses Theta((n + 1)*U) space including U subset containers and n*U/2 integer slots for n >= 1; n = 0 retains one empty subset. JavaScript sorting time T_sort(n) and auxiliary workspace S_sort(n) depend on the qualifying runtime; ECMAScript does not impose a universal sort complexity. Total time is O(T_sort(n) + (n + 1)*U), with O(n + 1 + S_sort(n)) auxiliary space including the copied sorted Array and excluding output. Qualify and charge the runtime sort implementation rather than treating it as free. U <= 2^n. Equal values are skipped only when index > start, eliminating duplicate sibling choices without forbidding a repeated value deeper in a subset. No constant-total-space claim is made.

helpers.name: collect
helpers.contract: A per-call recursive closure over ordered, path and subsets. Record a shallow path copy; skip an index only when it repeats its previous value at this same depth; otherwise choose, recurse from index + 1 and undo with pop. Sorting makes equal sibling choices adjacent while deeper recursion can retain permitted multiplicities.
helpers.cost: The complete nested helper definition is 329 UTF-8 bytes, including its indentation and terminal newline, and is charged in this standalone source. All invocations, copy operations, loop scans and push/pop updates are included in the stated output-sensitive cost; maximum live recursive depth is n + 1.

helpers.name: inline numeric sort comparator
helpers.contract: Compares two safe-integer Numbers by numeric ordering, returning -1, 0 or 1 without arithmetic on input values. Passed to sort only on nums.slice().
helpers.cost: The complete inline arrow-function body and the copy/sort call are included in total standalone source bytes. Each comparison is O(1); the qualifying runtime sort comparison count and workspace must be charged separately as T_sort(n) and S_sort(n).
